fatal_errors: The intervention is only described as generic high-pressure/high-temperature treatment rather than spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C.
No alloy composition is specified; the target is MgAlTiVFeCo ball-milled BCC powder.
The proposed temperature boundary below 700 °C excludes the target 800–1000 °C sintering window and the 1000 °C optimum.
The structural mediator is incorrectly assigned as a single-phase solid solution rather than densification and uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases such as AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3.
Corrosion and oxidation test environments are absent: 3.5 wt% NaCl and 900 °C air are required.
The evidence supports isolated concepts but does not establish that the proposed treatment improves compression, corrosion, and oxidation in the relevant MgAlTiVFeCo system.
The falsification experiment lacks a defined composition, pressure, dwell time, environmental controls, lower-temperature SPS comparators, and quantitative decision thresholds.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses suppression of brittle intermetallic behavior and names the three desired performance categories, but it does not reconstruct the material, intervention, processing window, or operative mechanism. Its high-pressure conversion-to-solid-solution concept is mainly extrapolated from Al55Mg35Li5Zn5, while the corrosion and oxidation citations concern different alloy systems and do not connect that phase conversion to the claimed environmental benefits. Predictions are qualitative and omit the target density, hardness, polarization parameters, and parabolic oxidation constants. The experiment is not strongly discriminating because failure is defined merely as absence of improvement, without specified controls or measurable thresholds.
